newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: South Korea rules out Fokker takeover.
newsitem.headline: South Korea rules out Fokker takeover.

text.p: The Dutch government said on Tuesday the South Korean government had ruled out a takeover of the bankrupt Dutch plane maker Fokker by a consortium led by Samsung Aerospace.
A spokeswoman told Reuters the government had received a communication to the effect that the takeover would definitely not proceed.
"We have received a fax in which they made their decision," she said, referring to a news agency ANP report on Tuesday which said the South Koreans had pulled the plug on the deal.
She said there were no further details on the decision.
As recently as December 23, Korean media sources were quoted as saying that Samsung Aerospace was still interested in buying the Dutch firm and that talks would re-start in the New Year.
But ANP said the consortium of potential buyers for Fokker, which also included Daewoo, Hyundai and Korean Air had now decided the problems involved are too great.
No-one at Fokker's receivers was available for comment.

The initial talks between the Fokker administrators, who have run the company since its bankruptcy in March, broke down in March after a series of deadlines passed with no firm word from the Koreans. The final straw came when Northern Ireland-based Shorts, part of Canada's Bombardier, said it would no longer supply wings for Fokker regional jets.

The Hague has indicated it might provide fresh capital for a new Fokker and invest in the development of a new 125-seater regional jet but Samsung was said to have baulked at demands for long-term job guarantees in the Netherlands.
Russia's Yakovlev said earlier this month it was still optimistic it could buy Fokker, citing a price of around $200 to $270 million, which it said it could pay with Russian government guarantees.
Fokker, founded in 1919 by Dutch aviation pioneer Antony Fokker, is one the oldest names in the industry. It went bankrupt in March after parent Daimler Benz withdrew crucial financial support.
